cases.semantic: A mutation using the exact live object generation is accepted by Cloud Storage.
Replaying the exact same execution request is recognized without a second object-generation mutation.
A mutation using an older object generation is rejected by Cloud Storage with HTTP 412.
A mutation using an unestablished future object generation is rejected by Cloud Storage with HTTP 412.
Two concurrent mutations against one generation permit exactly one Cloud Storage winner.
A stable idempotency key cannot be reused by a different execution identity.
An execution identity cannot change its request fingerprint while retaining the same stable idempotency key.
An already-applied execution identity cannot silently change its stable idempotency key.
An acknowledgement-discarded mutation is reconciled using read-back without blind replay, preserving point-in-time uncertainty.
Reconciliation distinguishes pre-application state from exact post-application state without treating absence as proof of non-commit.
